sentences.text: Shri Vivek Singh, learned counsel for the Petitioner .
Ms. Vinita Dwivedi, learned Panel Lawyer for the respon I.A. No.5716/2024, an application for urgent hearing is taken up for hearing and on due consideration the same is allowed.
2. Also heard on I.A. No.5715/2024, which is an application under Section 389 of Cr.P.C for suspension of sentence of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail, filed on behalf of the appellant.

3. The appellant has been convicted under Sections 419, 420, 468 & 471 of IPC,1860 and sentenced to undergo 03 years R.I., 7 years R.I., 7 years R.I. and 5 years R.I. with fine of Rs.500/- each of the sentence and usual default stipulations.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the learned trial Court has wrongly convicted the appellant without considering the evidence available on record.
The allegation against the appellant is that appellant Fundabai has misappropriated with one Suman and withdrawn money of Rs.85,000/- from the bank.
Later on, she herself admitted this fact before the bank and on that basis offence was made out.
The co-accused Ashok who is said to be husband of Sarpanch, has identified the appellant Fundabai Devda before the bank.
The misappropriated amount of Rs.85,000/- is involved in this case and that amount has already been deposited.
The appellant has already completed more than four months of his jail incarceration.
There are several omissions and contradictions in the statement of prosecution witnesses.
He further submitted that final hearing of this appeal is likely to take sufficient long time.
Under these circumstances, learned counsel prays that the application for suspension of sentence of the appellant be allowed.
5. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the application for suspension of sentence.
6 . Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, contention of learned counsel for the appellant, allegations and act of the appellant

, without commenting on the merits of the case, the Fundabai Devda vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133516766/
1 application is allowed and it is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if already not deposited, the appellant shall be released on bail, on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) in the like amount to the satisfaction of Trial Court, for his appearance before the Registry of this Court firstly on 22.08.2024 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
7. Application stands allowed and disposed of.
